primary_goal: Build authority for operational automation across UK SMEs while retaining ecommerce and wholesale as the strongest proof base.
ai_mention_rule: AI may be covered only when it supports controlled workflows, clear review rules and ROI proof.

articles.title: Should you integrate your systems or automate the hand-off?
articles.target_client_type: Operationally complex UK SMEs using two or more systems with repeated data movement between them
articles.industry_or_operating_context: Broader SME operations across ecommerce, wholesale, service and professional-services teams

rolling_12_portfolio_mix_after_publicati.note: Current published history remains heavily ecommerce-led; this article begins the planned shift towards an 8 broader / 4 core balance over future rolling windows.

articles.primary_buyer_problem: A team is repeatedly copying, cleaning or reconciling data between systems and does not know whether it needs a full integration, a lighter automation or a process fix.
articles.primary_search_intent: Compare system integration with workflow automation and decide which approach is appropriate.
related_query_family: should I integrate my business systems
articles.trend_or_durable_demand: Durable commercial demand. The decision recurs wherever SMEs use multiple operational systems and repeated exports, uploads, emails or reconciliations connect them.
articles.evidence_source_and_date: Current repository article gap audit completed 24 July 2026; no external trend was claimed because no dated external research was required for this durable decision topic.
articles.what_changed_or_matters: The site previously focused on specific ecommerce workflows. It lacked a broader decision page explaining when full integration is justified and when a controlled hand-off is safer and more economical.
articles.henry_distinct_contribution: A process and control perspective: choose the lightest safe solution after separating stable data transfer from human judgement, with stop rules and proof of payback.

overlaps_considered: Why stock sync fails between Shopify, Amazon and eBay
How to stop re-keying wholesale orders into Sage or Xero
Ecommerce AI automation: how to prove the ROI first
Your ecommerce operation should survive one person being away
rolling_12_article_audit.why_distinct: The article compares three solution architectures across broader UK SME operations. It does not diagnose one channel workflow, explain one finance task, focus on AI ROI or address key-person risk.

articles.original_editorial_asset: Five-row integration decision matrix comparing full integration, controlled automation and an improved manual process across frequency, input stability, failure cost, transformation need and likely fit.
articles.first_hand_contribution_or_limits: Uses Henry's proven process-design, data, control and ecommerce operating perspective. It does not claim first-hand experience in sectors beyond those stated.
articles.proof_points_used_recently: The 200,000-SKU and eight-hours-to-two-minutes proof points were deliberately not reused.
articles.readability_check: Passed by editorial review: short sentences, active voice and plain British English; designed to remain at or below grade 9.
articles.mobile_check: Passed conceptual checks at about 390px and 768px. The decision matrix collapses to labelled single-column rows; the article width and CTA remain fluid.
articles.ai_mention_check: Passed. AI is not used as a claim or selling point.

quality_rules: Write for operationally complex UK SMEs while retaining ecommerce and wholesale as the strongest proof base.
Every article must read at Hemingway grade 9 or lower.
Do not invent results, statistics, dates, names or testimonials.
Every article needs distinct intent and at least one original editorial asset.
AI is one controlled tool, never the offer or a replacement for judgement.
